00:00.270 --> 00:02.400
Max: Hey everyone, it's Max, and welcome.

00:02.400 --> 00:05.460
In this section we're going to learn about web scrapping.

00:05.460 --> 00:07.860
So before we jump in, let's just make sure we have all

00:07.860 --> 00:09.750
of the libraries installed that we're going to need.

00:09.750 --> 00:12.660
So the first one they need is requests.

00:12.660 --> 00:15.480
You can find it on this pypi.org website.

00:15.480 --> 00:17.370
You can just go into whatever search engine

00:17.370 --> 00:20.520
and just type in Python requests like this.

00:20.520 --> 00:23.310
And very easily, you should be able to find this website

00:23.310 --> 00:25.110
or you can just go to the URL here.

00:25.110 --> 00:26.760
And really all that we need is just

00:26.760 --> 00:29.040
to type in pip install requests.

00:29.040 --> 00:31.260
So I can click here to just copy this

00:31.260 --> 00:34.530
and we can go to our terminal or command line.

00:34.530 --> 00:35.700
Copy paste this in here,

00:35.700 --> 00:38.730
pip install requests, hit enter.

00:38.730 --> 00:43.110
That will take care of this installation for us, and yeah.

00:43.110 --> 00:44.640
Then the next thing that we're going to use

00:44.640 --> 00:46.620
is going to be Beautiful Soup.

00:46.620 --> 00:48.420
So what we're going to use requests for

00:48.420 --> 00:51.660
is basically it allows us to send these HTTP messages,

00:51.660 --> 00:52.890
which if you don't know what those are,

00:52.890 --> 00:54.060
don't worry about that so much,

00:54.060 --> 00:55.770
we'll talk about that a little bit.

00:55.770 --> 00:57.420
And essentially we're going to use this

00:57.420 --> 00:59.760
to kind of get started to seeing

00:59.760 --> 01:02.100
what data looks like when we, you know,

01:02.100 --> 01:03.270
request it from a website,

01:03.270 --> 01:06.480
when we try to access a website using Python.

01:06.480 --> 01:08.490
So that's what we'll use requests for.

01:08.490 --> 01:11.250
Beautiful Soup is specifically designed

01:11.250 --> 01:13.230
to make web scrapping easier,

01:13.230 --> 01:14.520
so it's going to make it much easier

01:14.520 --> 01:18.720
to deal with HTML tags and with XML format.

01:18.720 --> 01:22.050
And so yeah, we'll use requests to kind of, you know,

01:22.050 --> 01:24.690
get an understanding, but then we'll use Beautiful Soup

01:24.690 --> 01:26.667
to make our life a lot easier.

01:26.667 --> 01:28.980
And so to install Beautiful Soup,

01:28.980 --> 01:31.140
we're just going to copy this here,

01:31.140 --> 01:34.080
go into our terminal, and again, copy paste that,

01:34.080 --> 01:36.480
pip install Beautiful Soup 4,

01:36.480 --> 01:37.890
and it will just take care

01:37.890 --> 01:39.960
of the installation for us like this.

01:39.960 --> 01:42.960
And then finally, we're also going to use Selenium.

01:42.960 --> 01:45.480
Now Selenium is going to allow us

01:45.480 --> 01:48.690
to kind of emulate a web browser.

01:48.690 --> 01:50.520
And the reason that we're going to use this is

01:50.520 --> 01:55.080
because some websites load content with a script.

01:55.080 --> 01:57.450
So with both requests and Beautiful Soup,

01:57.450 --> 01:59.430
we're going to see just the static elements.

01:59.430 --> 02:02.280
So basically, anything that's kind of put there

02:02.280 --> 02:03.660
that's not being loaded.

02:03.660 --> 02:05.520
But as we'll see, some things, you know,

02:05.520 --> 02:07.890
they load and they're interactive.

02:07.890 --> 02:09.600
And to do that, basically we need

02:09.600 --> 02:12.480
to load up a web browser and interact with that.

02:12.480 --> 02:14.520
So we'll learn a lot more about that.

02:14.520 --> 02:17.040
But yeah, for that we're going to need Selenium.

02:17.040 --> 02:20.460
So again, we're on the pypi.org website.

02:20.460 --> 02:22.410
You can just find all of these easily either

02:22.410 --> 02:25.290
by going to the URLs up here or just by,

02:25.290 --> 02:26.940
you know, typing into your search engine,

02:26.940 --> 02:30.540
Python Selenium, Python Beautiful Soup, Python requests.

02:30.540 --> 02:32.550
But ultimately, what we're going to need

02:32.550 --> 02:36.480
to do is just copy this here, pip install Selenium.

02:36.480 --> 02:38.340
And we're going to paste that in here

02:38.340 --> 02:41.880
and that will take care of that installation for us.

02:41.880 --> 02:45.210
Now one more thing that we are going to need for Selenium is

02:45.210 --> 02:47.460
because we're going to basically be, you know,

02:47.460 --> 02:49.440
loading pages with web browsers,

02:49.440 --> 02:51.900
we need to also download a driver

02:51.900 --> 02:54.990
that we can use to, well, open that.

02:54.990 --> 02:57.270
So basically we want our programming language

02:57.270 --> 02:59.790
to open up a browser and kind of do all

02:59.790 --> 03:00.930
of the navigation for us,

03:00.930 --> 03:03.600
but all that's going to be done automatically.

03:03.600 --> 03:07.380
So to do that we're going to download a Chrome driver,

03:07.380 --> 03:12.380
and this way we can use Python to open up Chrome

03:12.390 --> 03:15.990
and navigate Chrome, but all of that,

03:15.990 --> 03:18.360
you know, automated and using Python.

03:18.360 --> 03:21.780
So go ahead and just download the latest Chrome driver

03:21.780 --> 03:24.450
from here, we'll talk more about this,

03:24.450 --> 03:25.800
how we can use this once we get

03:25.800 --> 03:28.080
to the dynamic web scrapping section.

03:28.080 --> 03:30.330
But yeah, just download a Chrome driver from here

03:30.330 --> 03:31.620
and you know, save it,

03:31.620 --> 03:35.850
and we'll get to that once we get to the dynamic part.

03:35.850 --> 03:38.610
Now, if you had some problems installing any of these,

03:38.610 --> 03:41.250
if pip doesn't work, and if you're using Anaconda,

03:41.250 --> 03:43.560
pip should still work.

03:43.560 --> 03:46.350
It could be that you need to use pip3 instead.

03:46.350 --> 03:48.390
This is especially true if you have multiple versions

03:48.390 --> 03:49.800
of Python installed.

03:49.800 --> 03:53.370
You may want to be using pip3 if you find

03:53.370 --> 03:55.380
that when you go into your code environment

03:55.380 --> 03:57.990
and you try to import requests, for example,

03:57.990 --> 04:00.120
that it's not importing, you should, you know,

04:00.120 --> 04:03.750
try to use pip3 instead to, you know,

04:03.750 --> 04:05.940
hopefully then that will take care of that.

04:05.940 --> 04:08.730
An easy way to check is if we just go into our terminal,

04:08.730 --> 04:11.550
if I type in which pip,

04:11.550 --> 04:13.800
then we can see here it's linked directly

04:13.800 --> 04:17.070
to my Anaconda 3, which is for Python 3.

04:17.070 --> 04:18.360
So if you type in which pip

04:18.360 --> 04:20.940
and if this is linked to like Python 2.7

04:20.940 --> 04:22.200
or something like that,

04:22.200 --> 04:24.210
or not if you're using Anaconda,

04:24.210 --> 04:25.830
of course, not to Anaconda,

04:25.830 --> 04:27.000
then it wouldn't be installed there.

04:27.000 --> 04:30.240
But usually by default this should, you know, all be true.

04:30.240 --> 04:32.730
Otherwise, you can also find the requests,

04:32.730 --> 04:34.920
the Beautiful Soup and Selenium,

04:34.920 --> 04:37.830
all using the conda install.

04:37.830 --> 04:39.570
It would probably be found on conda-forge.

04:39.570 --> 04:41.040
So it would be the same thing,

04:41.040 --> 04:44.550
just you know, Googling for Anaconda install request,

04:44.550 --> 04:46.650
Anaconda install Beautiful Soup 4,

04:46.650 --> 04:48.240
Anaconda install Selenium,

04:48.240 --> 04:50.280
and then rather than having pip install,

04:50.280 --> 04:51.900
you would have a conda install.

04:51.900 --> 04:52.800
But like I said,

04:52.800 --> 04:55.260
you're probably not going to have this issue,

04:55.260 --> 04:58.050
but just in case you are running into this,

04:58.050 --> 04:59.820
that would be the way to troubleshoot.

04:59.820 --> 05:01.650
First try doing pip3,

05:01.650 --> 05:03.630
and if you still can't import the libraries

05:03.630 --> 05:06.960
after you've restarted your Spyder environment,

05:06.960 --> 05:09.903
then try using conda install instead.

00:00.210 --> 00:02.730
Max: Hey, everyone, it's Max, and welcome.

00:02.730 --> 00:04.830
So for part of the web scrapping,

00:04.830 --> 00:07.230
since we're gonna be interacting with websites,

00:07.230 --> 00:09.660
it's important for us to know generally

00:09.660 --> 00:11.850
how websites are kind of structured,

00:11.850 --> 00:13.770
the things that go into them, basically,

00:13.770 --> 00:17.430
like HTML or XML and and kind of tags

00:17.430 --> 00:19.710
because ultimately, that's what we're gonna be using

00:19.710 --> 00:23.100
to navigate the website and extract data from it.

00:23.100 --> 00:26.490
So I've pulled up here the list of S&P 500 companies

00:26.490 --> 00:29.400
because this is one of the websites that we're gonna use

00:29.400 --> 00:33.270
when, you know, we're practicing throughout the lectures.

00:33.270 --> 00:36.690
And, well, to get a better sense or look

00:36.690 --> 00:40.830
at how this looks like, you can hit option Command + J

00:40.830 --> 00:42.630
if you're in Chrome and on a Mac,

00:42.630 --> 00:44.520
which will open up the Developer console here,

00:44.520 --> 00:46.350
and then you can go to the elements.

00:46.350 --> 00:51.350
Alternatively, you can right-click and do Inspect here.

00:52.080 --> 00:55.590
If you're not on Chrome, you can, well,

00:55.590 --> 00:57.240
all this is called the Developer console

00:57.240 --> 00:58.890
that we're looking to open,

00:58.890 --> 01:03.890
so you can go into the Help and just look for Developer,

01:04.440 --> 01:06.330
and oh, there we go.

01:06.330 --> 01:08.730
So here we can just do the Developer,

01:08.730 --> 01:10.650
and we can Inspect elements.

01:10.650 --> 01:13.260
So in Firefox, it should be the same, for example.

01:13.260 --> 01:15.660
You should just look to open the Developer console.

01:15.660 --> 01:17.790
I think in Firefox, it opens at the bottom,

01:17.790 --> 01:19.890
but you'll see a very similar thing,

01:19.890 --> 01:22.530
which is just, well, all of these tags here,

01:22.530 --> 01:26.700
the HTML head, body, and yeah,

01:26.700 --> 01:29.130
this is kind of how that structure looks like.

01:29.130 --> 01:31.350
We don't need to get too much into all this.

01:31.350 --> 01:33.000
It's important just for us to understand

01:33.000 --> 01:34.260
how the structure looks like,

01:34.260 --> 01:37.500
so an important thing to note is, for example,

01:37.500 --> 01:39.600
every time a section starts,

01:39.600 --> 01:44.430
we can see that it starts with these greater than,

01:44.430 --> 01:45.690
I'm sorry, the less than symbol,

01:45.690 --> 01:48.120
and then it has whatever, you know, the type is inside,

01:48.120 --> 01:52.560
and then you've got the greater than symbol here.

01:52.560 --> 01:54.000
And then you've got this stuff inside,

01:54.000 --> 01:56.280
and then you've got the same format,

01:56.280 --> 01:58.770
and then you've just got a forward slash here.

01:58.770 --> 02:00.270
So this basically means, you know,

02:00.270 --> 02:01.890
start whatever is inside here,

02:01.890 --> 02:04.590
and this means end whatever is inside here.

02:04.590 --> 02:09.210
And basically, anything inside here is then going to be,

02:09.210 --> 02:10.920
you know, the content inside.

02:10.920 --> 02:13.560
Additionally, we can see here that sometimes,

02:13.560 --> 02:16.440
we have this less than and then the name of, you know,

02:16.440 --> 02:19.440
whatever it is, and then before we get to the content,

02:19.440 --> 02:21.150
which is, well, we can go in here,

02:21.150 --> 02:22.470
and we can expand that in a second.

02:22.470 --> 02:26.940
Here, we've got some more information such as the class.

02:26.940 --> 02:28.890
Here, we can see that for the HTML tag,

02:28.890 --> 02:31.740
we've got the class name, the language,

02:31.740 --> 02:33.390
and just some other parameters.

02:33.390 --> 02:35.580
So there are all part of that definition,

02:35.580 --> 02:38.640
and this is also something that, you know, we can reference.

02:38.640 --> 02:41.190
And then, you can kind of think of this

02:41.190 --> 02:44.880
like a JSON structure or a Python dictionary structure,

02:44.880 --> 02:49.500
so our outside layer is going to be the HTML key,

02:49.500 --> 02:51.480
and then you open up another dictionary,

02:51.480 --> 02:53.850
and then inside, we've got the head and the body.

02:53.850 --> 02:56.610
And if we go into the body, let's expand that,

02:56.610 --> 03:00.450
we see we've got several, a div here,

03:00.450 --> 03:01.980
and we can close this,

03:01.980 --> 03:04.200
and so you can see this is how it's structured.

03:04.200 --> 03:06.540
And then, we can go further down into here,

03:06.540 --> 03:10.650
and, well, a nice thing about Chrome here we can see

03:10.650 --> 03:13.230
is that when we're hovering over these different sections,

03:13.230 --> 03:16.320
we can see what part, you know, that refers to.

03:16.320 --> 03:18.600
So let's say we wanna, well,

03:18.600 --> 03:21.180
dive down to this first intertext here,

03:21.180 --> 03:23.790
oh, keeps expanding, so we can go into the body.

03:23.790 --> 03:25.890
We'll hover over these different sections

03:25.890 --> 03:28.050
until that section is highlighted,

03:28.050 --> 03:29.880
and we can go down further.

03:29.880 --> 03:31.920
And here, we've got the intertext highlighted again,

03:31.920 --> 03:33.360
so we're gonna go into here,

03:33.360 --> 03:35.790
and this, again, highlights the intertext.

03:35.790 --> 03:36.960
Then, we can just keep going down,

03:36.960 --> 03:39.510
so we'll go expand into here.

03:39.510 --> 03:42.180
And then, we can see that essentially,

03:42.180 --> 03:44.280
this here is where we're gonna find

03:44.280 --> 03:48.120
all of that text inside of this p tag.

03:48.120 --> 03:50.730
So that's kind of how we can think about, you know,

03:50.730 --> 03:53.850
navigating this stuff, and it's just important

03:53.850 --> 03:56.610
for you to know that the structure is gonna be this,

03:56.610 --> 03:58.380
basically, this open and then a symbol,

03:58.380 --> 04:01.920
and then, we've got the close, and that indicates the start.

04:01.920 --> 04:03.540
You've got the content inside, and then,

04:03.540 --> 04:06.060
you've got the same thing with a forward slash here,

04:06.060 --> 04:07.920
which basically indicates that, you know,

04:07.920 --> 04:12.840
this section is now over and also that we're going down

04:12.840 --> 04:14.820
kind of in a hierarchical structure.

04:14.820 --> 04:16.230
So we've got the outside,

04:16.230 --> 04:19.560
and then, we're going inside HTML and then the body,

04:19.560 --> 04:21.840
and then here, we're going, so HTML, body,

04:21.840 --> 04:23.820
and then into this div,

04:23.820 --> 04:26.340
and so that's kind of how we're going down into that.

04:26.340 --> 04:28.980
So that's just kind of important to know that one,

04:28.980 --> 04:31.680
we have these tags, and these additional information is,

04:31.680 --> 04:34.560
like, class names or other types of names,

04:34.560 --> 04:37.710
and yeah, that we can go down and then go into HTML

04:37.710 --> 04:41.250
and then into the body and then into the div and so on.

04:41.250 --> 04:45.030
And through that, we can kind of navigate the website

04:45.030 --> 04:47.520
and kind of orientate ourselves based

04:47.520 --> 04:49.410
on this hierarchical structure

04:49.410 --> 04:51.483
and the tags that are used for it.

00:00.240 --> 00:02.430
Max: Hey, everyone. It's Max, and welcome.

00:02.430 --> 00:03.480
So in this lecture,

00:03.480 --> 00:05.850
we're gonna quickly talk about status codes

00:05.850 --> 00:07.050
that we can encounter.

00:07.050 --> 00:08.220
Since we're gonna be dealing

00:08.220 --> 00:11.133
with basically sending HTTP requests,

00:12.030 --> 00:14.760
we can't assume that we're always gonna get,

00:14.760 --> 00:15.960
basically everything is okay.

00:15.960 --> 00:18.660
Sometimes, we're gonna run into errors and problems.

00:18.660 --> 00:21.450
And to understand what type of problem we're dealing with,

00:21.450 --> 00:24.330
we basically get a status code,

00:24.330 --> 00:26.910
you know, returned along with our request.

00:26.910 --> 00:29.580
And, well, these are essentially the list

00:29.580 --> 00:31.110
of different status codes that they have.

00:31.110 --> 00:33.510
But you can see they're grouped into different categories.

00:33.510 --> 00:34.343
So you've got the,

00:34.343 --> 00:37.410
anything that starts with 1 is gonna be informational.

00:37.410 --> 00:40.620
Anything that starts with 2 is gonna be successful.

00:40.620 --> 00:42.000
So 200 is always great.

00:42.000 --> 00:43.560
That means everything's okay.

00:43.560 --> 00:46.170
3 is a form of redirection.

00:46.170 --> 00:48.090
4 is gonna be a client error.

00:48.090 --> 00:52.650
So a very, you know, famous one here is the 404 Not Found.

00:52.650 --> 00:55.800
And 5 is gonna be server side error.

00:55.800 --> 00:58.080
So just because we've encountered a problem

00:58.080 --> 01:00.180
when we're trying to contact websites,

01:00.180 --> 01:02.460
or APIs later on or anything,

01:02.460 --> 01:03.480
that doesn't always mean

01:03.480 --> 01:05.010
that it may be a problem on our side.

01:05.010 --> 01:08.160
Sometimes, it could be a problem on the server side,

01:08.160 --> 01:10.860
or we could have just written our requests wrong.

01:10.860 --> 01:13.440
So depending on what type of error there is,

01:13.440 --> 01:16.260
we're gonna get different response messages for it.

01:16.260 --> 01:18.390
So, for example, if we try to go

01:18.390 --> 01:22.470
to an invalid part of the Coding with Max website,

01:22.470 --> 01:26.310
we can go to like codingwithmax.com/test.

01:26.310 --> 01:28.290
Now, this doesn't exist.

01:28.290 --> 01:29.610
This is not a page here.

01:29.610 --> 01:34.260
And you can see up here we get a 404 Page not found error.

01:34.260 --> 01:37.530
And similarly, if we do that using,

01:37.530 --> 01:39.570
you know, sending a request in Python,

01:39.570 --> 01:43.560
we're also gonna get the status code 404 returned with it,

01:43.560 --> 01:44.393
which just means that

01:44.393 --> 01:47.283
whatever we were trying to access wasn't found.

00:00.090 --> 00:02.520
Max: Hey everyone, it's Max and welcome.

00:02.520 --> 00:04.890
So another important thing to cover

00:04.890 --> 00:06.760
before we then jump into web scrapping

00:06.760 --> 00:09.060
is gonna be handling errors.

00:09.060 --> 00:11.070
Now websites change over time

00:11.070 --> 00:12.750
and sometimes we make assumptions

00:12.750 --> 00:14.560
about the way that a website is formatted

00:14.560 --> 00:16.800
that may no longer be true.

00:16.800 --> 00:20.010
And so sometimes when we write a web scrap that works

00:20.010 --> 00:23.340
and the website changes, we're gonna encounter errors.

00:23.340 --> 00:26.140
And so that could mean that our program just crashes

00:26.140 --> 00:29.910
and we have to fix it and adapt it to the new situations.

00:29.910 --> 00:31.800
But if we have some web scraps running

00:31.800 --> 00:35.400
and we'd rather just, you know, when the errors come up,

00:35.400 --> 00:38.880
we kind of move on and try to get what we can still get

00:38.880 --> 00:42.300
because a lot of times it's not a full website revamp

00:42.300 --> 00:44.460
but rather just a small part here or there.

00:44.460 --> 00:45.870
And so it'd be better for us

00:45.870 --> 00:47.380
if we can continue to collect data

00:47.380 --> 00:49.590
and where the website's been changed,

00:49.590 --> 00:51.510
we're then gonna basically ignore that section

00:51.510 --> 00:52.840
and just add in missing values

00:52.840 --> 00:56.430
but we can still continue collecting data for the rest.

00:56.430 --> 00:58.830
So to deal with these types of errors

00:58.830 --> 01:01.830
where well, our program would otherwise crash,

01:01.830 --> 01:05.340
we can use error handling through try and accept

01:05.340 --> 01:07.230
which is just part of Python.

01:07.230 --> 01:09.360
So we'll take a quick look at that now.

01:09.360 --> 01:10.300
This is gonna be helpful

01:10.300 --> 01:13.320
so that we can avoid our program crashing

01:13.320 --> 01:15.390
just from like the smallest changes

01:15.390 --> 01:18.420
and that things are a little bit more robust.

01:18.420 --> 01:20.730
All right, so for example,

01:20.730 --> 01:24.570
let's write the following statement, print A.

01:24.570 --> 01:26.220
Now this is gonna cause an error

01:26.220 --> 01:27.990
because A isn't defined, right?

01:27.990 --> 01:30.510
We're not putting it in quotation marks as a string.

01:30.510 --> 01:34.320
So we've just got the variable A here, which isn't defined.

01:34.320 --> 01:36.510
So if we run this, we're gonna get an error

01:36.510 --> 01:39.420
which says, well, A is not defined.

01:39.420 --> 01:41.060
And we can see here the type of error

01:41.060 --> 01:43.110
is actually a name error.

01:43.110 --> 01:46.140
So that's whatever this is called.

01:46.140 --> 01:49.530
All right, so how can we deal with this?

01:49.530 --> 01:52.080

01:52.080 --> 01:54.510
where we're trying to look for something

01:54.510 --> 01:55.820
that may not be true

01:55.820 --> 01:58.260
or maybe a structure changes

01:58.260 --> 02:03.260
and we try to do something like string A divided by two

02:03.300 --> 02:05.310
because we assume something to be an integer

02:05.310 --> 02:06.540
but it's actually a string.

02:06.540 --> 02:08.520
And here we get a type error,

02:08.520 --> 02:10.440
which basically means, well,

02:10.440 --> 02:12.300
there's something wrong with the types that we're using.

02:12.300 --> 02:15.690
We can't divide a string by an integer.

02:15.690 --> 02:17.400
So how do we deal with these things?

All right, let's start with this

is gonna be stuff that we're going to try.

02:33.900 --> 02:36.000
And if anything in here breaks,

02:36.000 --> 02:41.000
then what comes along with the try statement is the except.

02:41.700 --> 02:46.700
And basically it's, we're gonna try everything in here

02:46.710 --> 02:48.480
and if something in here breaks,

02:48.480 --> 02:50.280
we're gonna go to the except statement

02:50.280 --> 02:52.230
and there we can do something else.

02:52.230 --> 02:54.820
So something that you can just do in the except statement

02:54.820 --> 02:56.610
is just put pass.

02:56.610 --> 02:58.740
So we can try the following

02:58.740 --> 03:00.390
and if it doesn't work,

03:00.390 --> 03:02.490
we're just not gonna do anything.

And what happens here when we do this,

03:04.770 --> 03:07.450
if we run this, we see it doesn't crash

03:08.300 --> 03:10.770
but it also didn't print out anything.

So what it does is it goes into this try statement.

03:13.520 --> 03:17.220
It tries to print out, well, the variable A.

03:17.220 --> 03:19.230
The variable A is not defined.

03:19.230 --> 03:20.420

03:20.420 --> 03:23.940
It gives us the name error here, which we saw before.

03:23.940 --> 03:26.070
But we're in the try statement

03:26.070 --> 03:28.680
and now because we've encountered an error,

03:28.680 --> 03:31.620
we basically go to the except statement instead.

03:31.620 --> 03:34.320
And all we do here right now is nothing.

03:34.320 --> 03:36.480
We just pass, we don't do anything.

03:36.480 --> 03:38.700
So if we have more code down here,

03:38.700 --> 03:42.600
we can see if we just say we're here now,

03:42.600 --> 03:44.340
then we're not gonna see anything.

03:44.340 --> 03:45.720
We're just gonna go in here.

03:45.720 --> 03:46.950
We're gonna encounter an error,

03:46.950 --> 03:49.110
go in here, not do anything

03:49.110 --> 03:51.390
and well, then we're here now.

03:51.390 --> 03:52.230
All right.

03:52.230 --> 03:54.330
So what happens if this partially succeeds?

03:54.330 --> 03:58.020
So let's first print out the string A

03:58.020 --> 03:59.970
or let's do AB not to confuse ourselves.

03:59.970 --> 04:01.980
And then we're gonna try to print out the variable A,

04:01.980 --> 04:04.020
which still doesn't exist.

04:04.020 --> 04:05.520
So we're gonna run this

04:05.520 --> 04:07.470
and we're gonna first print out AB.

04:07.470 --> 04:09.090
So this part succeeds.

04:09.090 --> 04:10.080
Then we're gonna go in here.

04:10.080 --> 04:12.090
We're gonna try to print out the variable A,

04:12.090 --> 04:13.110
which isn't defined.

04:13.110 --> 04:15.720
So again, we're gonna get the error that we saw before.

04:15.720 --> 04:18.020
Now, because part of the try statement failed,

04:18.020 --> 04:21.090
we're gonna go into this except part here.

04:21.090 --> 04:23.580
In the except part, we're not gonna do anything.

04:23.580 --> 04:25.590
So we just pass not doing anything.

04:25.590 --> 04:27.210
And then we just continue on

04:27.210 --> 04:30.800
and we print that we're here now.

04:30.800 --> 04:33.390
We can also do something in the except statement.

04:33.390 --> 04:34.800
For example, we can print here

04:34.800 --> 04:38.070
that we've encountered an error.

04:38.070 --> 04:39.990
So we can see that if we run this,

04:39.990 --> 04:44.070
we print AB, then this basically causes a crash.

04:44.070 --> 04:45.390
So we go to the except.

04:45.390 --> 04:47.340
Now, rather than passing, so doing nothing,

04:47.340 --> 04:50.340
we print that we've encountered an error.

04:50.340 --> 04:51.810
And then we continue on.

04:51.810 --> 04:53.740
And now we're here.

04:53.740 --> 04:55.350
You can also put those in loops.

04:55.350 --> 04:58.920
So you can say, if you have like a for loop here

04:58.920 --> 05:02.700
and we do this, we can see we're gonna print AB

05:02.700 --> 05:05.310
and then basically gonna continue to encounter errors.

05:05.310 --> 05:06.870
And then once our loop is done,

05:06.870 --> 05:08.490
we're gonna continue on with our code.

05:08.490 --> 05:10.800
So we can see that this just,

05:10.800 --> 05:13.100
we put this around whatever block of code

05:13.100 --> 05:15.540
may be encountering an error

05:15.540 --> 05:18.150
or may need to be considered differently.

05:18.150 --> 05:21.090
And it's all gonna work normally within our code,

05:21.090 --> 05:22.780
except that if we encounter an error

05:22.780 --> 05:25.050
within this try section here,

05:25.050 --> 05:27.180
we're gonna move on to the except.

05:27.180 --> 05:28.170
Now, an important thing to know

05:28.170 --> 05:31.500
is you can't have a try without an except.

05:31.500 --> 05:36.420
So we need an except statement.

05:36.420 --> 05:38.070
Let's take this out of the loop here.

05:38.070 --> 05:40.440
We need an except statement here

05:40.440 --> 05:42.570
or else we're also gonna have an error.

05:42.570 --> 05:47.220
So here it's, even if we put this inside of the try,

05:47.220 --> 05:51.810
here we're looking for the try.

05:51.810 --> 05:53.400
So, sorry, the except.

05:53.400 --> 05:58.400
So without the except, it's not going to work

05:58.410 --> 06:00.990
and we can see if we put the except back in here,

06:00.990 --> 06:02.970
everything will be fine.

06:02.970 --> 06:04.500
Now, what if we wanna know

06:04.500 --> 06:06.570
what type of error we encountered?

06:06.570 --> 06:07.920
Well, an easy way to do that

06:07.920 --> 06:09.990
is rather than just typing except,

06:09.990 --> 06:14.460
we can accept and then we have uppercase exception here

06:14.460 --> 06:17.880
as, and then we can just denote it as a variable.

06:17.880 --> 06:20.940
Usually it's just the variable E.

06:20.940 --> 06:23.580
And so what that does is we try the following.

06:23.580 --> 06:26.940
If it crashes, we go into the except statement,

06:26.940 --> 06:31.080
but we catch basically the information about the error.

06:31.080 --> 06:33.240
We save it in the variable E

06:33.240 --> 06:36.750
and then we can print out the string version of E.

06:36.750 --> 06:39.540
You're always gonna want to do the string version of E

06:39.540 --> 06:42.240
just in case sometimes this can cause problems.

06:42.240 --> 06:44.250
So always make sure to put string around it

06:44.250 --> 06:47.310
so that it doesn't crash inside of the except statement.

06:47.310 --> 06:48.270
So you're gonna try to,

06:48.270 --> 06:50.970
or you're gonna print out the string version of E.

06:50.970 --> 06:52.650
We can see if we run this,

06:52.650 --> 06:55.530
we can see first we go into the try,

06:55.530 --> 06:57.810
which is this AB here.

06:57.810 --> 07:00.030
Then we go in here, we encounter an error.

07:00.030 --> 07:01.590
We go to the except statement.

07:01.590 --> 07:04.260
Notice that we're not executing anything else down here.

07:04.260 --> 07:05.520
So we no longer print here now,

07:05.520 --> 07:07.410
even though this was outside first.

07:07.410 --> 07:09.000
We can see we don't continue on here.

07:09.000 --> 07:10.710
We go to the except.

07:10.710 --> 07:12.930
Now we store this error,

07:12.930 --> 07:15.510
this information about the error as E,

07:15.510 --> 07:18.120
and then we print out the information about the error.

07:18.120 --> 07:19.560
And so we can see here,

07:19.560 --> 07:22.230
the error is that name A is not defined.

07:22.230 --> 07:25.470
And if we scroll all the way up to the top,

07:25.470 --> 07:26.970
we can see here the first error,

07:26.970 --> 07:29.910
which is printing the variable A that's not defined.

07:29.910 --> 07:32.610
Again, we have the information here about the error,

07:32.610 --> 07:36.000
which is that name A is not defined.

07:36.000 --> 07:37.860
So yeah, this is how we can go

07:37.860 --> 07:40.230
about error handling in Python.

07:40.230 --> 07:41.940
It's useful for web scrapping

07:41.940 --> 07:43.140
when things can break easily

07:43.140 --> 07:44.760
because websites change and stuff.

07:44.760 --> 07:47.790
But of course, it's also useful in other parts of your code,

07:47.790 --> 07:49.950
especially when things are getting bigger

07:49.950 --> 07:52.260
and when there are a lot of things to consider,

07:52.260 --> 07:55.800
it's often good to kind of have these error handling cases

07:55.800 --> 07:58.590
so that when something does go wrong,

07:58.590 --> 08:02.640
especially if you're like in some kind of loop here

08:02.640 --> 08:06.180
for whatever, then you can print the exception out

08:06.180 --> 08:08.400
if you want to, you don't need to.

08:08.400 --> 08:12.030
Sometimes printing too much can actually cause an overflow.

08:12.030 --> 08:13.830
So sometimes you don't wanna print things out.

08:13.830 --> 08:16.530
And then you can just do here continue

08:16.530 --> 08:18.030
and basically continue on

08:18.030 --> 08:19.860
and the next part of the loop, for example,

08:19.860 --> 08:23.493
or you can do break or whatever else you want.

08:24.660 --> 08:28.110
So using these exception handling things in Python

08:28.110 --> 08:30.930
is very useful, of course, for web scrapping,

08:30.930 --> 08:33.460
but also generally when you're getting to bigger projects

08:33.460 --> 08:37.260
where there are many more cases for outliers or exceptions

08:37.260 --> 08:40.140
or all these types of things to occur,

08:40.140 --> 08:42.840
rather than having to write statements for every single one,

08:42.840 --> 08:46.120
you can kind of foolproof yourself or foolproof your system

08:46.120 --> 08:48.030
by if something does break,

08:48.030 --> 08:49.830
if something unexpected happened,

08:49.830 --> 08:52.170
then you're just gonna ignore that for now,

08:52.170 --> 08:55.200
Do whatever you need to do.

08:55.200 --> 08:56.700
Maybe if you're gathering data,

08:56.700 --> 08:58.800
just fill out that data with missing data instead

08:58.800 --> 09:01.983
and continue on rather than having your program crash.

Instructor: All right, the first thing

00:01.140 --> 00:02.610
that we're gonna be looking at here

00:02.610 --> 00:05.340
is going to be the modulus.

00:05.340 --> 00:09.990
So the modulus or the remainder pretty much tells us,

00:09.990 --> 00:12.210
or is a form of division that tells us

00:12.210 --> 00:14.970
how much we have as a remainder

00:14.970 --> 00:17.100
after we've completed the division.

00:17.100 --> 00:18.570
So for example,

00:18.570 --> 00:22.380
and I'm just gonna be working with print statements here,

00:22.380 --> 00:24.630
just so that we see everything on the output.

00:25.710 --> 00:27.150
So the first thing that we're gonna start with

00:27.150 --> 00:31.110
is going to be a modulus two.

00:31.110 --> 00:34.680
And we'll start off and we'll just go through

00:34.680 --> 00:35.550
a couple of numbers

00:35.550 --> 00:38.670
just so that we can really get a hang of what's going on.

00:38.670 --> 00:42.270
So for example, if we do a 0%2,

00:42.270 --> 00:44.580
we'll get a remainder of zero.

00:44.580 --> 00:49.580
If we do a 1%2, we'll get a remainder of one.

00:49.770 --> 00:53.340
And if we get a 2%2, we'll get a remainder of zero again.

00:53.340 --> 00:55.680
So we're kind of entering the cycle.

00:55.680 --> 00:58.560
And what's happening is that

00:58.560 --> 01:03.560
if I do some A%B, really what I'm doing is I'm dividing

01:07.140 --> 01:12.090
A by B, and then the output that I'm getting

01:12.090 --> 01:17.090
is going to be the remainder after the division.

01:20.700 --> 01:25.700
So in this case, for example, if I do 2/2,

01:27.030 --> 01:32.030
that gives me one with a remainder of zero, right?

01:33.420 --> 01:34.770
So we've divided 2/2,

01:34.770 --> 01:36.810
that gives me one with a remainder of zero.

01:36.810 --> 01:41.810
If I divide 3/2, for example, I get a one as an output here,

01:42.390 --> 01:47.390
3/2 gives me one, and then we've got a remainder of one.

01:50.010 --> 01:54.420
So we're dividing, so two fits once into three completely,

01:54.420 --> 01:56.370
and then we've got a one extra.

01:56.370 --> 01:59.370
And since one isn't bigger than two,

01:59.370 --> 02:02.460
we now have a remainder of two.

02:02.460 --> 02:06.660
If we were to do 5/2 instead, like this,

02:06.660 --> 02:11.660
we would get either one with a remainder of three,

02:12.870 --> 02:17.130
which would then be two with a remainder of one.

02:17.130 --> 02:19.470
Or you can just completely skip this step.

02:19.470 --> 02:23.700
So we see if we divide five by two,

02:23.700 --> 02:27.180
two fits in twice into five,

02:27.180 --> 02:29.430
and then we've got one leftover,

02:29.430 --> 02:33.840
and that's what we get with this modulus division.

02:33.840 --> 02:35.880
Now we can also do this for higher numbers,

02:35.880 --> 02:38.280
for example four.

02:38.280 --> 02:41.103
So if we do 5%4, we get one.

02:42.120 --> 02:45.060
If we do six, we're gonna get two.

02:45.060 --> 02:47.820
If we do seven, we're gonna get three.

02:47.820 --> 02:50.670
If we do eight, we're gonna get zero.

02:50.670 --> 02:51.990
So what we can see also

02:51.990 --> 02:54.390
that there is a kind of pattern going on.

02:54.390 --> 02:59.110
So if we do a modulus by a certain number A

03:00.600 --> 03:03.540
or a certain number B to be consistent with up here,

03:03.540 --> 03:08.540
we're gonna get numbers from zero up to B-1.

03:10.200 --> 03:13.290
So because if we get B

03:13.290 --> 03:16.260
and here that's just gonna give us one again.

03:16.260 --> 03:18.630
So this is kind of the abstract form, again,

03:18.630 --> 03:20.040
in the form of example.

03:20.040 --> 03:24.450
If we do a modulus of five,

03:24.450 --> 03:29.250
we can get numbers between zero, up to four.

03:30.420 --> 03:35.420
So we can get in here 0, one, two, three, and four.

03:37.020 --> 03:39.930
Because if we were to get five,

03:39.930 --> 03:42.300
then five divided by five

03:42.300 --> 03:45.030
gives us a remainder of zero again.

03:45.030 --> 03:47.760
So this is a nice way to also produce

03:47.760 --> 03:51.300
kind of cyclic numbers, especially if you're going in a row,

03:51.300 --> 03:53.190
and if you're doing modulus five,

03:53.190 --> 03:58.190
then 0, one, two, let's keep that format good here,

04:01.020 --> 04:06.020
0, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven,

04:09.960 --> 04:14.670
all that would go after doing a modulus five,

04:14.670 --> 04:15.810
we go to the following number.

04:15.810 --> 04:20.810
So we've got zero, we've got one, two, three, four,

04:21.660 --> 04:23.010
and then we'll start at zero again.

04:23.010 --> 04:24.840
And then we'll go one, two.

04:24.840 --> 04:27.930
So we see that we get kind of this cycle going on

04:27.930 --> 04:29.550
and that's really nice for us

04:29.550 --> 04:30.990
and we can use that to our advantage

04:30.990 --> 04:33.330
to kind of produce these cyclic numbers,

04:33.330 --> 04:36.000
especially if we're going just along

04:36.000 --> 04:39.933
a linear line of numbers.

it's kind of what we got returned.

All right, so let's try doing that.

So, the first thing that we want to know maybe

We can run that real quick,

of course what shows up here.

06:18.660 --> 06:21.960
So, let's run that one more time, and we can see here,

so we've got the previous close,

We've got, well even more,

this is actually the value that we want.

All right, cool, so now we've got

07:16.350 --> 07:20.070

07:20.070 --> 07:23.040
we can say, all right, so basically we know

07:23.040 --> 07:27.720

07:27.720 --> 07:29.470

All right, so we notice here is that we end with a span

07:55.080 --> 07:59.160
well, that ends somewhere else probably, right here.

08:12.450 --> 08:14.040

08:14.040 --> 08:18.420

08:18.420 --> 08:23.420

08:28.260 --> 08:31.950

08:31.950 --> 08:33.840

08:33.840 --> 08:36.360

08:36.360 --> 08:38.670
So, if we look at our reduced text

08:38.670 --> 08:42.270
and maybe just look at the first three elements

08:42.270 --> 08:45.273
because essentially we're just kind of splitting this all,

08:46.560 --> 08:47.850
let's print that out real quick.

08:47.850 --> 08:49.143
So we can see here, we've got a list now.

08:49.143 --> 08:52.920
Now, we've got a previous close is actually its own element

08:52.920 --> 08:55.920
because there's a span here where we split.

08:55.920 --> 08:59.430
Then we've got this part, which goes up to the next span,

08:59.430 --> 09:01.230
which actually ends here.

09:01.230 --> 09:03.990
And then we continue on and then we go the next part,

09:03.990 --> 09:06.000
which goes up to the next time

09:06.000 --> 09:09.780
that this span is encountered, all right?

09:09.780 --> 09:12.120
So, we notice when we're looking at this, okay,

09:12.120 --> 09:14.610
the value that we want is actually here.

09:14.610 --> 09:17.310
It's in the second element.

09:17.310 --> 09:20.370
So, the value that we want is gonna be the second element,

09:20.370 --> 09:22.650
which is the element with index one,

09:22.650 --> 09:23.880
since we start cutting at zero.

09:23.880 --> 09:25.500
So, this would be element zero.

09:25.500 --> 09:27.750
This is gonna be element one.

09:27.750 --> 09:29.910
So, that's where our goal value is.

09:29.910 --> 09:33.240
And our value that we actually want

09:33.240 --> 09:37.230
is in our reduced text, which is now just this,

09:37.230 --> 09:40.200
and it's going to be the part

09:40.200 --> 09:43.980
after this greater than symbol.

09:43.980 --> 09:45.680
So we're going to do another split

09:46.995 --> 09:49.230
and we're gonna split by this greater than,

09:49.230 --> 09:51.030
and we're gonna take the last element

09:51.030 --> 09:54.360
and that's where our value is going to be.

09:54.360 --> 09:57.840
So, if you print that out, we see now we have

09:57.840 --> 10:01.200
this value here, which is exactly this value here

10:01.200 --> 10:04.590
that we want, which corresponds to the previous close.

10:04.590 --> 10:07.290
All right, so of course, this is one way

10:07.290 --> 10:09.930
that you can go about, you know, web scrapping

10:09.930 --> 10:11.580
and extracting the data out.

10:11.580 --> 10:14.280
You can use, you know, all these indications that you have

10:14.280 --> 10:16.950
and kind of build a system based upon that.

10:16.950 --> 10:19.890
But we can see that it's kind of difficult

10:19.890 --> 10:22.050
because we have to go through the HTML

10:22.050 --> 10:24.720
and we have to find, you know, like the order

10:24.720 --> 10:26.670
and when these things occur

10:26.670 --> 10:29.550
and how the structure is doing the splitting.

10:29.550 --> 10:32.520
And it just takes a bit of time to, you know,

10:32.520 --> 10:34.980
go into the text, find the right location.

10:34.980 --> 10:37.470
It could actually be that previous close appear

10:37.470 --> 10:40.620
several times, and maybe the first previous close

10:40.620 --> 10:43.860
that we encountered isn't the right previous close.

10:43.860 --> 10:47.643
So, what we need to do there is basically loop.

10:48.960 --> 10:51.510
We could do, you know, some kind of loop here

10:51.510 --> 10:54.120
and then we could find the index.

10:54.120 --> 10:57.090
And if the index is not the right one, then we're gonna say,

10:57.090 --> 11:00.540
all right, our t is going to be everything from

11:00.540 --> 11:04.230
that index plus one, so that previous close is not included.

11:04.230 --> 11:06.480
And then we're gonna find the index again,

11:06.480 --> 11:08.070
which will get us to the next location.

11:08.070 --> 11:11.040
So, if this value pops up several times, you know,

11:11.040 --> 11:14.310
then we have to find wherever it is.

11:14.310 --> 11:17.160
If it's the second or third iteration, then we have to find

11:17.160 --> 11:18.600
that index first for it.

11:18.600 --> 11:21.150
So, we can see that this gets pretty complicated

11:21.150 --> 11:23.490
pretty quickly because it just requires

11:23.490 --> 11:24.810
some, you know, investigation.

11:24.810 --> 11:26.580
You need to go into the website, you need to see

11:26.580 --> 11:29.100
how it's structured, you need to see if you can find some

11:29.100 --> 11:32.160
of these rules, what kind of splits you can do.

11:32.160 --> 11:34.140
And of course, once you have this set up,

11:34.140 --> 11:37.830
then it works nicely until the website HTML has changed

11:37.830 --> 11:39.540
or the website structure has changed

11:39.540 --> 11:41.130
because of the structure here has changed

11:41.130 --> 11:44.310
and you know, there's no longer the span symbol used

11:44.310 --> 11:46.080
behind the number here.

11:46.080 --> 11:47.220
Then of course the code that we've

11:47.220 --> 11:49.350
implemented is not gonna work properly.

11:49.350 --> 11:51.690
So, you can see this is a way to go about it

11:51.690 --> 11:53.700
using the request library,

11:53.700 --> 11:57.390
but of course it's, you know, requires some manual work

11:57.390 --> 11:59.700
and well, all of web scrapping is gonna require this

11:59.700 --> 12:01.260
and you're always gonna be sensitive to these

12:01.260 --> 12:04.020
outside factors that are outside of your control,

12:04.020 --> 12:06.390
but here we're just working a lot with text

12:06.390 --> 12:08.700
and processing text and you know,

12:08.700 --> 12:11.550
trying to find these patterns that we can use

12:11.550 --> 12:13.650
to then, you know, make these assumptions,

12:13.650 --> 12:16.350
which is for example, that the span is afterwards.

12:16.350 --> 12:19.470
And then through that we can get our values,

12:19.470 --> 12:20.880
but we can see that this works

12:20.880 --> 12:23.640
and we can of course get the rest of all

12:23.640 --> 12:25.860
of these values out here if we want to too,

12:25.860 --> 12:29.610
using the same approach, but it's difficult.

12:29.610 --> 12:32.850
So, what we're gonna do is use Beautiful Soup,

12:32.850 --> 12:36.150
which is designed specifically to help us, you know,

12:36.150 --> 12:38.460
reduce some of these or deal with some of these problems

12:38.460 --> 12:41.970
to make all of this dealing with HTML easier,

12:41.970 --> 12:44.430
especially because it comes in this nice format

12:44.430 --> 12:47.280
where you know, one thing is contained within the other

12:47.280 --> 12:49.140
and all that sort of stuff.

12:49.140 --> 12:52.320
So, Beautiful Soup is there to basically help us

12:52.320 --> 12:54.240
and make our life easier with that.

12:54.240 --> 12:56.760
But of course, you know, you can use the request approach,

12:56.760 --> 13:00.270
but now we're gonna look at how can we do this cleaner

13:00.270 --> 13:02.043
using Beautiful Soup.

when you're building web scrapper,

05:40.043 --> 05:42.270

05:42.270 --> 05:43.470
You know, we may just have to go

05:43.470 --> 05:45.801
to a different element here.

05:45.801 --> 05:50.476
All right, so right now we have access to this element,

05:50.476 --> 05:53.640
and if we print it out, then we get this.

05:53.640 --> 05:56.040
But actually, if we wanna just access

05:56.040 --> 05:57.900
some of the text inside so we can see here,

05:57.900 --> 06:01.080
there's a bunch of just extra information.

06:01.080 --> 06:03.600
There is a class name going on here,

06:03.600 --> 06:05.970
we've got this variable declared here,

06:05.970 --> 06:09.510
the React ID for the data, and some all this other stuff.

06:09.510 --> 06:10.461
But really the only text

06:10.461 --> 06:12.390
that's contained within all of this

06:12.390 --> 06:16.417
is the previous close here and this value here.

06:16.417 --> 06:19.061
So if we wanna access the text elements,

06:19.061 --> 06:22.560
we can go into .text, and we're gonna get

06:22.560 --> 06:24.870
a text element returned, or actually,

06:24.870 --> 06:26.490
both of the text elements in this case,

06:26.490 --> 06:28.620
and they're gonna be joined together like this.

06:28.620 --> 06:30.393
All right, so that's pretty nice.

06:31.500 --> 06:33.600
This is one way that we can get out these values,

06:33.600 --> 06:35.430
but of course we're gonna have to go through them,

06:35.430 --> 06:37.230
then we're gonna have to look at a way

06:37.230 --> 06:39.000
that we can automatically separate this

06:39.000 --> 06:42.510
and we may know the value so we can just, you know,

06:42.510 --> 06:44.880
look for the previous close, and then after that

06:44.880 --> 06:45.870
take out this element.

06:45.870 --> 06:49.242
So that's one way to go about it, but for educational sakes,

06:49.242 --> 06:52.230
let's look at some different ways of taking this further

06:52.230 --> 06:54.083
because, you know, you may not always be

06:54.083 --> 06:56.656
in exactly this situation.

06:56.656 --> 06:59.950
Now, what's so cool about BeautifulSoup

06:59.950 --> 07:03.090
is that when we access an element here,

07:03.090 --> 07:04.680
we can actually do a lot more with it.

07:04.680 --> 07:06.671
So for example, here we notice, okay,

07:06.671 --> 07:11.552
so both our name, the previous close, and the value

07:11.552 --> 07:15.051
are also contained within this TD tag.

07:15.051 --> 07:16.290
And you'll say, yeah,

07:16.290 --> 07:17.968
of course they're also contained within the span tag,

07:17.968 --> 07:19.990
but let's start with the TD first.

07:19.990 --> 07:21.170
Okay, so we can go in here

07:21.170 --> 07:26.170
and we can actually access these TD tags like this.

07:26.460 --> 07:30.491
So what we'll do is, in this case,

07:30.491 --> 07:35.491
we're actually going in, and we go to the first TD tag,

07:35.643 --> 07:39.810
and goes all the way up to here.

07:39.810 --> 07:41.334
So we can see all of this

07:41.334 --> 07:44.010
is just extracted for us like that.

07:44.010 --> 07:47.130
So we can actually follow this hierarchical structure

07:47.130 --> 07:50.070
if we go back to the developer console

07:50.070 --> 07:51.605
so we can see we go into the TR tag,

07:51.605 --> 07:56.605
and now we've gone into this TD tag, and basically,

07:56.940 --> 08:00.090
now we've accessed this value here.

08:00.090 --> 08:04.022
And so here we can see again, we can access the text,

08:04.022 --> 08:06.930
and here it's just going to be

08:06.930 --> 08:09.646
the previous close in this case because well,

08:09.646 --> 08:12.039
we've gone directly into the TD, and of course,

08:12.039 --> 08:16.890
we can go even deeper and we can go into either TD,

08:16.890 --> 08:20.212
and then from the TD into the span to get the text,

08:20.212 --> 08:25.212
but we can actually also just directly jump into the span,

08:25.530 --> 08:30.010
and it's gonna get this first span keyword here

08:30.010 --> 08:31.290
that it finds.

08:31.290 --> 08:34.620
All of these are gonna be the previous close value.

08:34.620 --> 08:37.620
So that's pretty great, you know, that's one way

08:37.620 --> 08:40.380
that we can go in here and at least get this value out,

08:40.380 --> 08:42.566
but now you'll be like, all right, you know, wait a minute,

08:42.566 --> 08:47.566
this here, our values are also contained within the TD tag.

08:48.030 --> 08:51.600
But when I use the TD tag here, we can see that, you know,

08:51.600 --> 08:54.390
we're only getting the first value returned.

08:54.390 --> 08:57.840
How can we go about getting the other ones?

08:57.840 --> 09:00.790
All right, so what we can do here

09:00.790 --> 09:05.790
is we can access the contents like this,

09:07.107 --> 09:12.107
and so that's gonna return basically every kind of subsystem

09:12.870 --> 09:16.680
that we have here, again, in a list format.

09:16.680 --> 09:21.600
Okay, so essentially we've got our TR tag,

09:21.600 --> 09:23.880
and each of the contents is then this kind of

09:23.880 --> 09:28.050
this own separate block inside.

09:28.050 --> 09:31.779
So now we can again go into say, element zero,

09:31.779 --> 09:34.453
and here we can access the text,

09:34.453 --> 09:37.110
which is gonna be our previous close,

09:37.110 --> 09:38.670
which we've had before.

09:38.670 --> 09:40.660
But if we go into the second element

09:41.520 --> 09:45.054
and access the text there, then this is actually gonna be

09:45.054 --> 09:48.480
the number that we're looking for here.

09:48.480 --> 09:50.156
So we can see that this is a really nice way

09:50.156 --> 09:54.300
that basically every single one of these blocks

09:54.300 --> 09:57.058
contained with inside this one TR block here,

09:57.058 --> 10:00.480
if we look at the content, it's again, split up into lists.

10:00.480 --> 10:01.739
And so that way, it's really easy

10:01.739 --> 10:04.170
to kind of navigate through these different ones.

10:04.170 --> 10:06.470
And again, if we access, you know, this tag,

10:06.470 --> 10:09.990
either the TD or the span, it's only ever gonna take us

10:09.990 --> 10:13.084
to the first one that it finds and start using the content.

10:13.084 --> 10:16.132
That's an easy way to find, you know,

10:16.132 --> 10:18.720
the things that we're looking for.

10:18.720 --> 10:20.981
Now, you may also notice that right now

10:20.981 --> 10:22.980
here we have class names,

10:22.980 --> 10:25.950
and there's also like this data test variable here

10:25.950 --> 10:28.170
is declared with the previous close value,

10:28.170 --> 10:31.432
and these are also indications to us that, you know,

10:31.432 --> 10:33.531
this is where our data is.

10:33.531 --> 10:35.820
It's contained within here.

10:35.820 --> 10:38.280
Now the class names here are actually not clean at all.

10:38.280 --> 10:40.297
They're pretty bad, but some websites

10:40.297 --> 10:42.193
the class names are extremely clean,

10:42.193 --> 10:44.940
and all of these things may have similar names,

10:44.940 --> 10:46.650
which is like information.

10:46.650 --> 10:49.050
So like here, these ones could called, you know,

10:49.050 --> 10:52.380
like, name or whatever, and then this one

10:52.380 --> 10:55.470
could be like, name, value, or, you know, whatever.

10:55.470 --> 10:56.940
The class names could be a lot cleaner,

10:56.940 --> 11:01.080
and you'll probably find that in some of the HTML tags

11:01.080 --> 11:03.330
or in the HTML codes that you're looking at

11:03.330 --> 11:04.714
for different websites.

11:04.714 --> 11:06.760
So another thing that you could do

11:06.760 --> 11:11.760
is when you do this find all, you can actually also

11:11.850 --> 11:15.780
kind of look based on specific class names.

11:15.780 --> 11:19.620
So you can say here, okay, we're looking for the class

11:19.620 --> 11:21.480
that has the name,

11:21.480 --> 11:25.263
and maybe we'll just take this name for now.

11:26.310 --> 11:28.650
Let's see, where does it end?

11:28.650 --> 11:33.650
Here, and let's copy paste that in here.

11:35.796 --> 11:38.070
Missing an underscore here.

11:38.070 --> 11:40.402
So let's try that one more time.

11:40.402 --> 11:42.450
Okay, there we go.

11:42.450 --> 11:47.450
So in this case, it did not find what we're looking for,

11:48.870 --> 11:51.330
and that's because the class name here

11:51.330 --> 11:52.650
does not correspond to TR.

11:52.650 --> 11:54.180
It corresponds to TD.

11:54.180 --> 11:56.343
Let's try that one more time.

11:56.343 --> 11:58.770
All right, so now we can see that we've got

11:58.770 --> 12:00.434
basically all of the TD tags

12:00.434 --> 12:04.441
that have this class name returned, and of course,

12:04.441 --> 12:08.940
well, this is not extremely clean, but, you know,

12:08.940 --> 12:11.640
we can see that everything here, each of these

12:11.640 --> 12:15.143
is if we just look at the first element,

12:15.143 --> 12:18.024
is going to be this TD tag,

12:18.024 --> 12:23.024
and the class name is the following here.

12:23.100 --> 12:25.222
So if these class names are a bit cleaner,

12:25.222 --> 12:27.390
and in this case it does look like, you know,

12:27.390 --> 12:28.983
the names are all contained within here,

12:28.983 --> 12:30.960
but the class names themselves

12:30.960 --> 12:32.559
don't really tell us that much.

12:32.559 --> 12:35.910
So you can use them, but you may also find

12:35.910 --> 12:36.864
that for different websites,

12:36.864 --> 12:40.290
the class names are actually very straightforward,

12:40.290 --> 12:43.293
and so they're very easy to kind of navigate.

12:44.490 --> 12:45.690
But yeah, this is one way

12:45.690 --> 12:49.260
that we can also filter for class names if we want to.

12:49.260 --> 12:51.582
Let's go back to our TR,

12:51.582 --> 12:56.582
and maybe we can just leave this in here for reference,

12:57.080 --> 13:00.744
but then going back to our TR splits

13:00.744 --> 13:03.644
looking at the first value again.

13:03.644 --> 13:06.570
All right, so something else that we notice

13:06.570 --> 13:10.950
is we've got a different tag here, which is,

13:10.950 --> 13:12.504
where is it here?

13:12.504 --> 13:13.337
This data test.

13:13.337 --> 13:18.337
So if we wanna look for maybe a specific tag here,

13:18.630 --> 13:22.500
which in this case again, is this data test tag

13:22.500 --> 13:24.450
which has the previous close value,

13:24.450 --> 13:27.990
what we can also do is we can go in, and in this case,

13:27.990 --> 13:32.190
we can actually, again, use this find all method,

13:32.190 --> 13:35.170
and because if we're looking at the one element

13:35.170 --> 13:37.590
and we're only gonna get one element return,

13:37.590 --> 13:39.845
we actually have to use find instead of find all.

13:39.845 --> 13:42.001
So we're gonna use find.

13:42.001 --> 13:46.136
This time, we're gonna look for the TD tag,

13:46.136 --> 13:49.754
and we're gonna define the attribute

13:49.754 --> 13:53.594
or the attributes that we're gonna be looking for,

13:53.594 --> 13:58.224
and we're gonna say, all right, we want to find

13:58.224 --> 14:01.380
where the data test attribute

14:01.380 --> 14:05.943
has the value of this one here.

14:07.560 --> 14:10.923
All right, and let's run that.

14:12.210 --> 14:16.350
Okay, so now we can see we've got this element extracted,

14:16.350 --> 14:18.329
this TD class element extracted

14:18.329 --> 14:21.630
where the data test value here

14:21.630 --> 14:23.790
is equal to the previous close value.

14:23.790 --> 14:25.236
So again, we're searching by names,

14:25.236 --> 14:30.236
and then here, once again, we can also access the text

14:31.710 --> 14:33.630
to get this value out here.

14:33.630 --> 14:35.970
So again, these searching features, you know,

14:35.970 --> 14:38.010
right now aren't so useful to us

14:38.010 --> 14:42.201
because we found a very easy way to get out these values,

14:42.201 --> 14:44.760
which is using this.

14:44.760 --> 14:46.678
If we just go into the first element again

14:46.678 --> 14:51.000
and print out the contents, we can see

14:51.000 --> 14:52.941
that we can very easily go read these contents

14:52.941 --> 14:55.169
and just go into each of them,

14:55.169 --> 14:57.840
and basically print out the text,

14:57.840 --> 15:00.546
which is gonna give us the text that we want,

15:00.546 --> 15:03.599
and we can do the same thing going to the second element

15:03.599 --> 15:07.242
and giving us the text that we want here.

15:07.242 --> 15:10.920
But of course, you know, that's specific to this website,

15:10.920 --> 15:12.570
and the thing about web scrapping

15:12.570 --> 15:15.150
is that all websites are kind of built up differently.

15:15.150 --> 15:18.210
You've got different developers that use different formats,

15:18.210 --> 15:20.580
and sometimes you have some templates being used

15:20.580 --> 15:23.700
like on WordPress, or Squarespace, or stuff like that,

15:23.700 --> 15:25.227
you know, so some things follow templates,

15:25.227 --> 15:27.142
other websites are built from scratch,

15:27.142 --> 15:30.598
other websites are built in some intermediate way.

15:30.598 --> 15:33.630
So you're gonna encounter a lot of different HTMLs.

15:33.630 --> 15:34.770
Some is gonna be good,

15:34.770 --> 15:36.277
and some is gonna be really nicely structured,

15:36.277 --> 15:37.539
and you're gonna look at it

15:37.539 --> 15:39.309
and it's gonna be very easy to follow.

15:39.309 --> 15:43.104
Others is gonna be mediocre, others is gonna be chaotic,

15:43.104 --> 15:45.090
so the thing with web scrapping

15:45.090 --> 15:47.013
is you're gonna have to be very prepared

15:47.013 --> 15:49.590
that, you know, every website is gonna be different,

15:49.590 --> 15:51.392
every web scrap is going to be different,

15:51.392 --> 15:54.363
and so you need to be able to adapt to those situations.

15:54.363 --> 15:56.490
So the important things to know

15:56.490 --> 15:58.552
are being able to filter by these tags,

15:58.552 --> 16:02.526
specifically being able to look for specific class names.

16:02.526 --> 16:05.460
If values are only contained, you know,

16:05.460 --> 16:07.184
within specific class names,

16:07.184 --> 16:09.584
being able to look for custom attributes.

16:09.584 --> 16:14.584
So this data test here is a custom attribute

16:15.270 --> 16:18.013
that's being defined here with this value.

16:18.013 --> 16:20.471
So being able to filter specifically for those,

16:20.471 --> 16:22.980
how to access the text here,

16:22.980 --> 16:24.990
being able to go through these different contents,

16:24.990 --> 16:29.342
and also just being able to go into our HTML here,

16:29.342 --> 16:32.670
and, you know, basically seeing, okay,

16:32.670 --> 16:35.283
there's like this hierarchal structure that I can follow,

16:35.283 --> 16:38.610
and we've got these TR tags, you know,

16:38.610 --> 16:41.212
which contain all of these values that I can see here,

16:41.212 --> 16:45.480
and that I can go in here and we've got more TD tags.

16:45.480 --> 16:47.130
Basically, you know, that we can go in

16:47.130 --> 16:48.690
with each of these and knowing,

16:48.690 --> 16:50.040
okay, this is where I can find

16:50.040 --> 16:51.210
the value that I'm looking for,

16:51.210 --> 16:53.310
but especially if we're looking for aggregate,

16:53.310 --> 16:55.543
you know, like this whole column or both of these

16:55.543 --> 16:58.155
essentially this whole table of values here,

16:58.155 --> 17:01.170
going beyond just looking for one value,

17:01.170 --> 17:02.520
but, you know, trying to figure out,

17:02.520 --> 17:04.770
okay, what is the pattern that I can use

17:04.770 --> 17:06.480
to get out these specific values?

17:06.480 --> 17:09.030
Now, some websites will make it easier for you

17:09.030 --> 17:11.940
by having good structure, and basically,

17:11.940 --> 17:13.950
you can just iterate over these things

17:13.950 --> 17:15.704
and extract out all the values.

17:15.704 --> 17:18.013
Some websites are gonna be extremely messy,

17:18.013 --> 17:20.340
and you may just have to write, you know,

17:20.340 --> 17:22.635
like a custom thing where you find

17:22.635 --> 17:25.020
each of these individual values

17:25.020 --> 17:27.033
and just extract the data from them

17:27.033 --> 17:30.243
because there's no pattern that you could find,

17:30.243 --> 17:32.280
and maybe you could have spent a lot of time

17:32.280 --> 17:34.920
looking for a pattern, but also just writing,

17:34.920 --> 17:39.920
you know, like, navigating to each of these elements here

17:40.080 --> 17:42.270
using our code like this also wouldn't take too long.

17:42.270 --> 17:44.720
It's just a little bit more manual labor intensive,

17:44.720 --> 17:46.980
but it also wouldn't take too long.

17:46.980 --> 17:49.230
Of course, you know, this would really suck

17:49.230 --> 17:52.662
for having high numbers of, you know, entries here.

17:52.662 --> 17:56.280
So web scrapping is a lot, you know,

17:56.280 --> 18:00.180
being able to kind of find these patterns on your own.

18:00.180 --> 18:01.620
Also, of course, you know,

18:01.620 --> 18:02.956
did the website have a good developer

18:02.956 --> 18:04.773
that makes the structure a lot easier.

18:04.773 --> 18:07.710
So it's in and of itself also, you know,

18:07.710 --> 18:09.453
a lot of problem solving involved,

18:09.453 --> 18:12.720
and you kind of have to approach the website and see

18:12.720 --> 18:14.435
okay, how is it structured,

18:14.435 --> 18:17.478
and how can I use that structure to my advantage

18:17.478 --> 18:22.140
to most easily get out the data that we're looking for?

18:22.140 --> 18:25.050
And so in this way, we've seen several, you know,

18:25.050 --> 18:26.824
different ways of getting out the data.

18:26.824 --> 18:31.824
One easy way that we found is just by splitting everything,

18:33.154 --> 18:38.154
or finding all these TR tags going into them,

18:38.790 --> 18:40.027
splitting it up by the contents,

18:40.027 --> 18:42.403
and here it's actually really nicely organized

18:42.403 --> 18:44.280
that each of these contents

18:44.280 --> 18:47.304
is itself kind of this contained within this TD tag.

18:47.304 --> 18:51.390
One contains the name of the stat,

18:51.390 --> 18:53.490
and the other one contains the stat itself.

18:53.490 --> 18:55.800
We could also be unlucky that there's a third thing here

18:55.800 --> 18:57.150
with some garbage inside,

18:57.150 --> 18:58.909
in which case we would need to take care of that.

18:58.909 --> 19:00.491
But right now it's actually really clean

19:00.491 --> 19:02.940
that we only have essentially the two values

19:02.940 --> 19:04.173
that we're looking for, which is the name

19:04.173 --> 19:07.508
and the target value or the stat.

19:07.508 --> 19:08.878
So again, if we run this

19:08.878 --> 19:12.630
and now we can just access these differently or separately,

19:12.630 --> 19:14.062
we can see here, okay, one is the name,

19:14.062 --> 19:16.897
and the other one is going to be our stat.

19:16.897 --> 19:18.629
And so in this way, it's really easy

19:18.629 --> 19:23.629
to kind of get out these values from this website here.

19:24.403 --> 19:28.140
But again, I wanna point out that this is not,

19:28.140 --> 19:30.570
this structure is not gonna be true for all websites, right?

19:30.570 --> 19:33.396
This is true for this specific website here,

19:33.396 --> 19:36.510
and so the big part of web scrapping

19:36.510 --> 19:38.610
that we've done here is just going in,

19:38.610 --> 19:40.989
figuring out the format, and trying to find the best way

19:40.989 --> 19:44.223
to get out this information that we're looking for here.

11:48.808 --> 11:50.700

12:15.411 --> 12:19.410

12:19.410 --> 12:22.472

12:22.472 --> 12:27.389

12:30.300 --> 12:32.520
because you wanna be as safe as possible.

12:32.520 --> 12:33.900

12:33.900 --> 12:35.880

12:35.880 --> 12:38.190
So if you put everything inside of

12:38.190 --> 12:40.590

12:40.590 --> 12:43.020

12:43.020 --> 12:44.940

12:44.940 --> 12:46.483

Whereas if we have the try and except statements in here,

12:49.251 --> 12:52.829

13:22.349 --> 13:23.709
and stuff like that.

13:23.709 --> 13:26.880
So again, also different things that you can do with the try

13:26.880 --> 13:29.940

13:29.940 --> 13:31.512

13:31.512 --> 13:35.550
what assumptions you've made and how your data is structured

13:35.550 --> 13:36.960
and all those types of things.

13:36.960 --> 13:40.344
But we can see here that the elements that we're using

13:40.344 --> 13:43.226
to extract the data is actually really nice, right?

13:43.226 --> 13:45.630
We're just creating our beautiful soup object.

what we could say is, okay,

14:31.770 --> 14:33.810

At the end of the day, the important thing is

15:10.109 --> 15:13.140

15:13.140 --> 15:15.949

15:15.949 --> 15:19.590

15:19.590 --> 15:22.008

15:22.008 --> 15:25.512

15:25.512 --> 15:28.967

15:28.967 --> 15:32.220
And then also sometimes you're just gonna need to come back

15:32.220 --> 15:33.928

15:33.928 --> 15:37.029

15:37.029 --> 15:41.446

15:41.446 --> 15:44.790

15:44.790 --> 15:47.090

15:47.090 --> 15:51.390

15:51.390 --> 15:52.710

15:52.710 --> 15:54.328
Did the website data change?

15:54.328 --> 15:56.580
Can I see the value on the website?

15:56.580 --> 15:58.410
If yes, why is it not included?"

15:58.410 --> 15:59.520
So those are a lot of the things

15:59.520 --> 16:01.651
that go into this web scraping stuff.

16:01.651 --> 16:04.980

16:04.980 --> 16:06.570

16:06.570 --> 16:09.832

16:09.832 --> 16:12.487

16:12.487 --> 16:15.030

17:11.629 --> 17:13.091

17:15.891 --> 17:19.267

17:19.267 --> 17:21.990

17:24.150 --> 17:27.480

17:37.512 --> 17:41.149

Max: Hey, everyone, it's Max, and welcome.

So in this video, we're gonna look at the challenging part

00:05.400 --> 00:09.120

00:09.120 --> 00:10.260

00:10.260 --> 00:13.740
is make the scrap run every 15 seconds,

00:13.740 --> 00:17.850
check if our file exists to not overwrite it,

00:17.850 --> 00:20.160
and add an additional field to track

00:20.160 --> 00:22.290
when the data was collected.

00:22.290 --> 00:27.000
All right, so to make it run every 15 seconds,

00:27.000 --> 00:30.000
we're going to import the time library.

00:30.000 --> 00:32.550
Now, I've told you the libraries or the modules

00:32.550 --> 00:34.530
that we need to use in the exercise sheet,

00:34.530 --> 00:38.400
I've also given you the functions that we needed to use.

00:38.400 --> 00:41.160

00:41.160 --> 00:44.280

00:44.280 --> 00:46.920
to use one extra feature that you haven't dealt with

00:46.920 --> 00:48.897
or you haven't dealt with in a longer time.

00:48.897 --> 00:51.810
And then you just need to go online and see an example

00:51.810 --> 00:53.310
and, you know, see how it works

00:53.310 --> 00:55.260
and then implement that into your current code.

And so the point of this challenge part of the exercise

01:00.780 --> 01:05.490
like realistic part where it's very likely that you're going

01:05.490 --> 01:08.610

01:08.610 --> 01:11.820
to your situation, or as time evolves, you know,

01:11.820 --> 01:14.520
extra modules come out that you may want to use.

01:14.520 --> 01:16.260
And so being able to deal with all of that

01:16.260 --> 01:19.710
is also an important part of like being a data scientist,

01:19.710 --> 01:23.400
being able to, you know, use new modules that may help you

01:23.400 --> 01:25.710
and make your life a lot easier.

01:25.710 --> 01:30.520
All right, so first, making it run every 15 seconds.

01:30.520 --> 01:35.040
Okay, so what we can start out with is, first of all,

01:35.040 --> 01:40.040
we wanna have a start time, so we can use this time.time

01:40.920 --> 01:42.990
to get the current epoch's time

01:42.990 --> 01:47.130
and then we can save that in this start time.

01:47.130 --> 01:51.570
Now what we can do is we can save this time.

01:51.570 --> 01:55.270
So for example, if we import time here

01:56.280 --> 01:59.280
and we have our start time here,

01:59.280 --> 02:03.600
and then if we do time.time minus start,

02:03.600 --> 02:05.730
then it takes the current time

02:05.730 --> 02:09.810
and it subtracts it at whatever time this was saved

02:09.810 --> 02:12.240
and we basically get a time difference.

02:12.240 --> 02:15.600
So we can see this is how many seconds

02:15.600 --> 02:18.180
since we've declared this variable.

02:18.180 --> 02:21.810
And so we can use that to then, you know,

02:21.810 --> 02:25.230
combining with this time.sleep,

02:25.230 --> 02:27.540
which basically makes your program wait

02:27.540 --> 02:30.000
for however many seconds you put in here.

02:30.000 --> 02:32.760
So let's say we make it sleep for one second,

02:32.760 --> 02:35.580
it will run for a second, basically waiting,

02:35.580 --> 02:39.270
and then it will continue on.

02:39.270 --> 02:42.090
All right, so what we wanna do is,

02:42.090 --> 02:44.940
to make a run every 15 seconds, we can put this,

02:44.940 --> 02:47.340
for example, into an infinite loop.

02:47.340 --> 02:50.610
We can say, while true, do the following.

02:50.610 --> 02:53.580
So then we wanna collect the current time.

02:53.580 --> 02:58.580
Then here, we want to extract and save data and,

03:00.270 --> 03:01.820
which is basically all of this,

03:03.300 --> 03:05.220
although we are gonna need to change some of those up,

03:05.220 --> 03:06.300
let's take away these comments

03:06.300 --> 03:08.970
to make our code cleaner again.

03:08.970 --> 03:13.970
So here, we want to check current time.

03:16.800 --> 03:19.290
Then we wanna extract and save the data.

03:19.290 --> 03:24.290
And then we want to wait until 15 seconds have passed

03:26.070 --> 03:29.430
from above and then basically continue.

03:29.430 --> 03:33.630
So what we wanna do, and let's just fill in this last part

03:33.630 --> 03:38.070
in here first, is we want to sleep

03:38.070 --> 03:43.070
for whatever is the current time minus the start time,

03:44.790 --> 03:47.640
so let's probably do this outside, it's better.

03:47.640 --> 03:52.640
So the time difference is the current time

03:52.920 --> 03:54.630
minus the start time, so that's gonna be

03:54.630 --> 03:56.040
the time difference.

03:56.040 --> 04:00.750
And basically, we wanna sleep for 15 seconds

04:00.750 --> 04:04.230
minus the time difference.

04:04.230 --> 04:05.760
And the reason that we wanna sleep for this

04:05.760 --> 04:10.050
is let's say that we start at just one second

04:10.050 --> 04:11.880
and then the whole program runs,

04:11.880 --> 04:14.100
it does the whole data extraction and saving,

04:14.100 --> 04:17.310
and now it's at two seconds, these are, well,

04:17.310 --> 04:18.930
these times don't really make that much sense

04:18.930 --> 04:21.060
'cause this is relative to like the 1970s,

04:21.060 --> 04:23.070
but let's just use one or two as an example,

04:23.070 --> 04:27.660
then one second will have passed, so two minus one is one.

04:27.660 --> 04:30.720
So that means if we wanna make it run every 15 seconds,

04:30.720 --> 04:35.490
we then need to sleep for 15 minus the time difference.

04:35.490 --> 04:38.520
So there's one more extra thing that we need to do though,

04:38.520 --> 04:41.880
and as you can see that, when I was running this code,

04:41.880 --> 04:44.610
this code can take longer than 15 seconds to run.

04:44.610 --> 04:48.330
So to make this run, you know,

04:48.330 --> 04:51.270
to not basically have this be like inconsistent

04:51.270 --> 04:54.150
if our time difference is bigger than the 15,

04:54.150 --> 04:58.620
we wanna say, okay, if 15 minus the time difference

04:58.620 --> 05:03.620
is greater than zero, then we want to sleep for this amount.

05:06.030 --> 05:09.720
Otherwise, if we've already passed 15 seconds

05:09.720 --> 05:13.530
just from doing the extraction and the saving,

05:13.530 --> 05:17.640
then we can just continue on with the next iteration.

05:17.640 --> 05:19.320
So we're only gonna do this

05:19.320 --> 05:24.000
if our time difference is smaller than 15 seconds,

05:24.000 --> 05:28.230
and then we're gonna basically wait until the remaining part

05:28.230 --> 05:31.230
of the 15 seconds are up and then we're gonna continue on,

05:31.230 --> 05:35.760
and again, we've put this in an infinite loop so, you know,

05:35.760 --> 05:37.500
the way that we're gonna kill it at the end

05:37.500 --> 05:39.720
or that we're gonna stop the program

05:39.720 --> 05:43.410
is either by having it crash, which is not that great,

05:43.410 --> 05:47.280
or by forcing it to stop by just basically interrupting it,

05:47.280 --> 05:50.160
so if we have it in here, we can interrupt it in here,

05:50.160 --> 05:51.780
or if we're running it somewhere else,

05:51.780 --> 05:54.090
we can then also just interrupt the process there.

05:54.090 --> 05:56.310
But this infinite loop is basically gonna make it

05:56.310 --> 05:59.670
go on forever unless, you know,

05:59.670 --> 06:02.460
you somehow force the program to stop, another way

06:02.460 --> 06:05.280
is like shutting down the machine or something like that.

06:05.280 --> 06:06.420
Okay, so that's the first part,

06:06.420 --> 06:09.270
which is making it run every 15 seconds.

06:09.270 --> 06:11.820
Now the second part is gonna be checking

06:11.820 --> 06:16.170

06:16.170 --> 06:19.950

06:19.950 --> 06:21.870

06:21.870 --> 06:23.610

06:23.610 --> 06:25.560
and we're only looking at one thing right now,

06:25.560 --> 06:29.370
which is just checking if the file exists or not.

06:29.370 --> 06:32.220
So what we're gonna do is we can check, all right,

06:32.220 --> 06:37.220
if os.path.isfile, and then we just need to put our path

06:38.460 --> 06:43.080
in here in a second, then we'll do something.

06:43.080 --> 06:45.483
Here, we want to don't overwrite,

06:46.470 --> 06:50.490
otherwise, we want to create.

06:50.490 --> 06:53.280
So to make all of this more consistent,

06:53.280 --> 06:56.640

06:56.640 --> 07:00.540

07:00.540 --> 07:04.007

07:06.750 --> 07:11.750
if the file exists, the file at this location,

07:12.150 --> 07:14.340
then we don't want to overwrite it.

07:14.340 --> 07:19.340
So what we can do is we can use, we can still save it

07:19.893 --> 07:24.330
to a CSV, we can make the mode append mode,

07:24.330 --> 07:27.600
and we can set the header parameter to false.

07:27.600 --> 07:32.250
Now, this is important because we're basically adding it

07:32.250 --> 07:34.890
on extra then, and setting the header to false

07:34.890 --> 07:37.440
is also important because otherwise, every time we save

07:37.440 --> 07:42.000
to the CSV, we're also going to get the header part saved,

07:42.000 --> 07:43.170
and we don't want that, right?

07:43.170 --> 07:44.970
Once we have the header in there once,

07:44.970 --> 07:48.450
we don't wanna save the header again every single time

07:48.450 --> 07:49.713
we've extracted data.

07:51.330 --> 07:54.000
And so setting the header to false

07:54.000 --> 07:58.290
is basically gonna make sure that that doesn't happen.

07:58.290 --> 08:01.500
Now, another thing that we can do if we wanna be safe

08:01.500 --> 08:05.580

So let's continue on with now,

basically looking at this chart here

and just looking at one thing

and seeing how we can't get that using requests

00:12.780 --> 00:15.240

00:15.240 --> 00:17.580

00:17.580 --> 00:20.200
what exactly are we doing and how can we use that

00:20.200 --> 00:22.840
and when should we use dynamic web scraps

00:22.840 --> 00:25.050
and all that sort of stuff.

00:25.050 --> 00:28.050
But all right, so first of all, we need to take the URL.

00:28.050 --> 00:31.290
So we'll copy this, put that in here.

00:31.290 --> 00:34.440
This one's a long one, but that's all right.

So this symbol should read, let's see,

01:10.980 --> 01:13.380
if, oh, maybe we'll just go into the page source

01:14.760 --> 01:16.263
and look for it.

So this would be BTC dash is what it starts with.

So let's see if we can find this BTC dash USD

01:37.320 --> 01:38.523
using requests.

01:39.420 --> 01:40.830
All right, so we've got our requests

01:40.830 --> 01:44.047
and then we're gonna say if it's BTC dash USD,

if value in t, print yes,

All right, so we're just checking

So we'll run this, wait for this to run for a second here

02:07.200 --> 02:09.750
and no, it's not inside, which is weird

02:09.750 --> 02:12.120
because we can see it on the website.

02:12.120 --> 02:15.540
However, this stuff was kind of, it was loaded for us.

02:15.540 --> 02:19.710
So this is not something that is kind of a normal part

02:19.710 --> 02:22.800
of the HTML, it's we go to the website,

02:22.800 --> 02:25.260
this stuff is loaded and then it appears.

02:25.260 --> 02:27.030
Whereas what we do with requests

02:27.030 --> 02:29.940
is we basically take the first picture,

02:29.940 --> 02:32.040
the first snapshot of the website.

02:32.040 --> 02:33.000
So we go to the website

02:33.000 --> 02:36.150
and we just get the first thing that's shown.

02:36.150 --> 02:37.740
None of this stuff is shown initially,

02:37.740 --> 02:40.500
all this stuff is loaded or most of the stuff is loaded,

02:40.500 --> 02:42.270
which is why we're not gonna see any of this

02:42.270 --> 02:43.770

02:43.770 --> 02:45.500
So what Selenium allows us to do

02:45.500 --> 02:50.010
is we can actually create our own or not create,

02:50.010 --> 02:52.500
it will use the web driver.

So in this case, it will use Chrome

02:54.480 --> 02:56.430

02:56.430 --> 02:59.490

02:59.490 --> 03:01.680

So let's see how we can set that up.

03:04.320 --> 03:07.540
We're gonna create our web driver

03:07.540 --> 03:09.750

03:09.750 --> 03:12.120
